questions.skill: Justify that the inscribed triangle is equilateral
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Points A, B, C, D, E, F are marked around a circle with center O by stepping the radius. Prove that triangle ACE is equilateral.
questions.prompt_markup: Points A, B, C, D, E, F are marked around a circle with center O by stepping the radius. Prove that triangle ACE is equilateral.
questions.required_method: Show each central angle between consecutive marks is 60°, so AOC, COE, EOA are each 120°, then use congruent triangles (SAS).
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof. Essential: each small triangle (O, two consecutive marks) is equilateral, so each central angle is 60°; ∠AOC = ∠COE = ∠EOA = 120°; triangles AOC, COE, EOA are congruent by SAS (radii); so AC = CE = EA.

questions.prompt: Compass and straightedge only; leave all arcs. Construct a regular 12-sided polygon inscribed in the circle.
questions.prompt_markup:
Compass and straightedge only; leave all arcs.

questions.correct_answer: Mark six points by stepping the radius, then bisect each of the six arcs (perpendicular bisector of each chord) to get six more; join the 12 points in order.
